sentences.text: The supervisory architecture separates station-wide observation from local bay and protection functions.
The Station Supervisory Control System is named Glasswing in this document.
The Station Supervisory Control System presents available station and bay indications through a consolidated operator interface.
Its displays show operating conditions and communication quality without replacing local equipment indications.
The Station Gateway carries supervisory communications between station-level functions and remote operations interfaces.
Supervisory visibility depends on the availability and quality of the underlying communications and status inputs.
The supervisory layer does not perform the protective functions assigned to dedicated protection equipment.
The Control Room Operator uses the supervisory displays to assess station conditions and coordinate operating actions.
Any supervisory command remains subject to configured permissions and the applicable operating procedure.
Local interlocks and equipment-level control logic remain authoritative for permitted switching actions.
A communications interruption can leave displayed information stale or temporarily unavailable.
After communications recover, operators confirm that indications are current before relying on them for decisions.
The Satellite Time Receiver is named Bluefin in this document.
The Satellite Time Receiver acquires a reference from supported satellite timing signals.
It distributes time to station equipment over the configured time-distribution network.
Time distribution supports consistent event timestamps across equipment that receives and applies the reference.
Accurate timestamps assist event correlation but do not establish the validity of an electrical measurement or protection decision.
If the external timing reference is lost, equipment behavior depends on its individual clock and holdover capabilities.
Holdover performance varies by device and may degrade as the interval without a valid reference increases.
The Satellite Time Receiver produces the Clock Drift Snapshot when its measured offset meets the configured reporting condition.
Time-quality indications allow operators to distinguish synchronized operation from degraded or unavailable timing.
The Station DC System supplies operating power to station automation equipment within its designed capacity.
A loss of station power can interrupt supervisory visibility and time distribution until supported supplies are restored.
The Station Supervisory Control System produces the Alarm Acknowledgement Slip for supervisory recordkeeping.
The Substation Supervisor oversees operational use of the supervisory system and escalation of unresolved availability concerns.
